Definition: middle voice from G1722 and κομβόω (to gird); to engirdle oneself (for labor), i.e. figuratively (the apron as being a badge of servitude) to wear (in token of mutual deference):--be clothed with.
BiblicalUsage: Peter tells all of us to be clothed with humility in 1 Peter 5:5 — to gird ourselves with it like a servant's apron — for God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe humility is something I put on, not something I feel — an apron I tie on every morning before I serve anyone.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
